title: Good and Poor Conductors of Heat
seo_title: Primary 4 Science: Conductors and Insulators of Heat Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 4: Energy forms and uses (Heat: good and poor conductors of heat)
standard_text: Identify good and poor conductors of heat and relate their uses to everyday life, such as cooking pots, handles, oven gloves and cooler boxes. Investigate how well different materials conduct heat in fair tests (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on good and poor conductors of heat: metals, wood, plastic, styrofoam and air, uses, and fair-test experiments. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Metals conduct heat well; wood and plastic do not.
key_sub: Poor conductors keep hot things hot and cold things cold.
body_html:
How to think about it

Heat flows through some materials quickly and through others slowly.

  • Good conductors of heat: metals such as copper, aluminium and steel. Used for pots and baking trays.
  • Poor conductors of heat: wood, plastic, rubber, cloth, styrofoam and air. Used for handles, oven gloves and cooler boxes.
  • Poor conductors keep hot things hot and cold things cold, because they slow down heat flow in both directions.
  • A metal object feels colder than wood at the same temperature because it takes heat from your hand faster.
Example

Why is a frying pan handle made of plastic?

Plastic is a poor conductor of heat

Little heat reaches your hand

Answer: So the handle stays cool.

Example

Wax on a copper rod melts before wax on a glass rod. Which is the better conductor?

Heat reached the wax faster on copper

Answer: Copper.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a metal object in the same room is colder than a wooden one. Both are at the same temperature.
  • Thinking blankets and clothes give out heat. They slow down heat loss from your body.
  • Thinking poor conductors only keep things hot. They also keep cold things cold.
  • Thinking air is a good conductor. Trapped air is a poor conductor.

faq.q: Which materials are good conductors of heat?
faq.a: Metals such as copper, aluminium, iron and steel. Heat flows through them quickly.

faq.q: Why does metal feel colder than wood in the same room?
faq.a: Both are at the same temperature. Metal conducts heat away from your hand faster, so it feels colder.

faq.q: Can a poor conductor keep things cold?
faq.a: Yes. A styrofoam cooler box slows down heat flowing in from the warm air, so the drinks inside stay cold longer.
